name: Laser
description: Renders a laser beam between two points.

fields.description: The render settings for the laser.

name: Lightning Beam
description: Renders a fluctuating lightning between two points.

fields.description: The render settings for the lightning.
The amount of segments the lightning should have.
Time until the lightning changes its shape.
The spread of the lightning fluctuation. It defines how "far" the lightning can spread out from the core

name: Textured
description: Renders a beam between two points using a custom texture.

fields.description: The texture to use for the beam.
The size/diameter of the beam.
The initial rotation of the beam in degrees.
The rotation speed of the beam.
The render type to render the beam with.
The light emission of the beam. Must be within 0 - 15

name: Flat Textured
description: Renders a beam between two points as a flat texture that always faces the camera. The texture is repeated along the beam and never stretched; the last repetition is cut off if the remaining length is shorter than one tile.

fields.description: The texture to use for the beam.
The size of one texture tile: width of the beam and length of one repetition along it.
The render type to render the beam with.
The light emission of the beam. Must be within 0 - 15

name: Segmented Textured
description: Renders a beam as flat textured layers around one axis that can tile, spin and scroll. Can sag near the origin and tighten over "sag_duration". Good for drill or corkscrew beams.

fields.description: The texture layers to render simultaneously around the beam axis, each either a sweeping ribbon ("facing": "radial", default) or a stack of flat cards facing down the beam ("along_beam").
The render type to render the beam with.
The light emission of the beam, from 0 to 15.

How far, in blocks, the beam bows sideways from a straight line when loose, at its most bowed point near the origin. Both ends always stay pinned to their anchors. 0 (default) keeps the beam perfectly straight.
How many full side-to-side wave cycles the sag has along the beam, fading from full strength at the origin to none at the target. Only matters when "sag_amplitude" is above 0.

Ticks for the beam to go from loose to taut after it starts being drawn for an entity. It starts loose again after a fresh attach (e.g. a new swing or grapple). Only matters when "sag_amplitude" is above 0.
Tints every texture layer by the color a registered source reads off an item in "slot" (first match wins). "source" is an id an addon registered; with no match it stays white. Omit for no tint.

name: Boxed Textured
description: Renders a beam as a stack of textured boxes like palladium's "textured" renderer, but each face has its own lighting normal. That fixes wrong or flickering brightness on side and bottom faces.

fields.description: The texture applied to each box segment.
The cross-section size of each box segment, in blocks.

How many blocks of beam one full copy of the texture covers, separate from "size". Keeps the arm's thickness fixed while you control how dense the texture is. Defaults to the average of "size"'s width and height.
A fixed rotation, in degrees, around the beam's own axis.
Degrees per tick to continuously spin the boxes around the beam's own axis.
The render type to render the beam with.
The light emission of the beam, from 0 to 15.

name: Glow Laser
description: Palladium's laser beam with brightness settings for its glow and core. Below 1 fades the part, above 1 stacks extra draws for a stronger glow (up to 8). Both are values, so molang can animate them.

fields.description: The render settings for the laser, exactly as for palladium:laser.
How bright the glow is. 1 is the laser as Palladium draws it.
How bright the core is. 1 is the laser as Palladium draws it.

name: Cone
description: Draws a beam as a cone from "start_size" to "end_size" blocks wide, with a soft glow, a brighter core and an optional scrolling texture. Pair it with the "cone" setting of argon:energy_beam.

fields.description: How wide the cone is where it starts, in blocks.
How wide the cone is where it ends, in blocks.

If set, "end_size" is reached this many blocks from the start and the cone keeps that angle however long the beam is, so a beam stopped by a wall is narrower. Set it to the ability's max_distance. Without it, "end_size" is the width wherever the beam ends.
The soft outer glow: its colour (hex), its opacity (0 turns it off) and its width compared with the whole cone's. Drawn as "glow_layers" nested cones.
The brighter core inside the glow, set the same way.
How many nested cones the glow is made of (1-8): more is softer and thicker toward the middle.
A texture over the cone's surface. Keys: texture*, color, opacity (0.6), scale (1), texture_length (2), around (2), scroll_speed (0.03), rotation_speed (0).
How the cone is blended into the scene: additive glows brighter where layers overlap, translucent is a plain see-through surface.
How opaque the far end of the cone is compared to the start, 0 to 1. Lower fades the cone out along its length.
How many flat sides the cone is drawn with (6-64): more is rounder.

name: Ring
description: Draws a flat textured disc around the start of the beam, as wide as the beam is long, with bands that travel outward like shockwave rings. Only the beam's length matters, so it suits argon:anchored_beam, whose animation_timer fades it in and out.

fields.description: The ring texture. Its U axis runs around the ring and its V axis outward.
A color multiplied with the texture.
How opaque the ring is, 0 to 1.
Radius of the empty hole in the middle, in blocks.
How many blocks outward one repeat of the texture covers.
How many times the texture repeats around the ring.
How many texture repeats the bands travel outward per tick; negative pulls them inward.
How many degrees per tick the ring spins.
How many degrees the ring is twisted between its inner and outer edge, which curves the bands into spirals.
How opaque the outer edge is compared with the inner one, 0 to 1.
How far above the start of the beam the ring is drawn, in blocks.
How the ring is blended into the scene.
How many flat sides the ring is drawn with (8-96).
If true, the ring faces along the beam instead of lying flat, so it works as a circle in front of a hand.
